newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-AMERICANS COULD SWEEP WOMEN'S MEDALS IN LAUSANNE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-AMERICANS COULD SWEEP WOMEN'S MEDALS IN LAUSANNE.

text.p: The prospect of an American sweep of the women's medals looms large at the world figure skating championships this week even with doubts about the form of titleholder Michelle Kwan.
By her own admission Kwan is going through a rough patch, having ceded her United States national title and her Champions' Series crown to 14-year-old Tara Lipinski in the past month.
Still, predictions are widespread of a U.S. sweep to match the one by Kristi Yamaguchi, Tonya Harding and Nancy Kerrigan in Munich six years ago.
"I think with the skaters of the quality we have, the U.S. have a great chance to go 1-2-3," Lipinski's coach, Richard Callaghan, said on Wednesday.
The event begins on Friday and ends on Saturday afternoon.

Lipinski, so mature for one so young, has a chance to become the youngest ever champion of the event after being 15th last year while Nicole Bobek, 19, is over her early season back problems and seems to be skating better than when she won bronze two years ago in Birmingham, England.

That leaves Kwan as the only doubt and no-one seriously believes that the girl who won so spectacularly in Edmonton last year could finish out of the medals this time no matter what setbacks she has suffered recently.
"I went through a bad patch and I'm struggling to get back," Kwan conceded at a U.S. team news conference on Wednesday.

At least she can joke about it, referring to the "coma" she has been in. Her coach, Frank Carroll, was quick to disagree. "Michelle has been in seven competitions this season and won five and was second twice. That's hardly a 'coma' year," he said.
"But perhaps she has been thinking too much and not just doing it," he added, saying that it was typical of many skaters to have trouble defending titles.
"I don't think winning so much last season affected my head," Kwan said. "But I am trying to get my mental edge back.
"My last two competitions have been a little shaky," added the 16-year-old Californian, who had won 10 of her final 11 competitions heading into last month's nationals.
Her problems began during the free programme at the nationals, where she scaled a triple toe loop-triple toe loop combination down to triple-double and then fell on the landing.
Then she put one hand down on a triple flip, fell on a triple loop and did only a double lutz.
"I panicked after the first fall when I wasn't concentrating," she said at the time.
Both her programmes at the Champions' Series final included falls but at least she stood up during her qualifying skate here on Monday.
"I will tell myself that this is just another competition," she said.
The women who threaten American domination are having problems of their own.

Chen Lu, the Chinese who chased Kwan all the way to the gold medal last year, is by her own admission out of the medals hunt because of a foot injury that cost her four months of training until a month ago.
And European champion Irina Slutskaya, third last year, looks to be struggling with her weight and finished only third in her qualifying group on Monday.
At least she has not given up the chase.
"Today my objective was only to qualify," she said on Monday.
"I can skate much better. I am here to win the final."
